records.title: Every game piece has an owner.
records.text: 1.7. Every game piece has an owner. Every game piece in play also has a controller.

records.title: You “own” the pieces you bring to the game (your deck, side deck, Gig dice, etc.).
records.text: 1.7.1. You “own” the pieces you bring to the game (your deck, side deck, Gig dice, etc.). You’re the “owner” of these pieces.

records.title: You “control” the pieces currently in your friendly Gig area, field, Legends area, and Eddies area.
records.text: 1.7.2. You “control” the pieces currently in your friendly Gig area, field, Legends area, and Eddies area. You’re the “controller” of these pieces, even if you’re not the owner.

records.title: Pieces you control are considered “friendly” pieces.
records.text: 1.7.2.1. Pieces you control are considered “friendly” pieces.

records.title: Pieces your Rival controls are considered “rival” pieces.
records.text: 1.7.2.2. Pieces your Rival controls are considered “rival” pieces.

records.title: Game pieces can change controllers, but can never change owners.
records.text: 1.7.3. Game pieces can change controllers, but can never change owners.

records.title: When you take control of a Rival’s game piece, follow the rules in {GOLDEN RULES > Respect Your Rival}.
records.text: 1.7.3.1. When you take control of a Rival’s game piece, follow the rules in Respect Your Rival.

records.title: At the end of the game, return all game pieces to their respective owners.
records.text: 1.7.3.2. At the end of the game, return all game pieces to their respective owners.

records.title: Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.
records.text: 2.3. Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.

records.title: If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.
records.text: 2.4. If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.

records.title: A game value can be a negative number.
records.text: 2.10. A game value can be a negative number.

records.title: When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
records.text:
2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Unit has 2 power. An effect reduces its power by 3. The Unit has -1 power, but is treated as having 0 power when attacking, fighting, or when a card effect references its power. If it then gains +2 power, that Unit has 1 power. The order of these effects being applied does not alter this outcome.

records.title: A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number.
records.text: 2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

records.title: “Face-down” refers to a card displaying its back.
records.text: 3.4. “Face-down” refers to a card displaying its back.

records.title: While a card is face-down, ignore all card information, except whether or not the card is a Legend.
records.text: 3.4.1. While a card is face-down, ignore all card information, except whether or not the card is a Legend. (As indicated by the cardback design.)

records.title: “Ready” refers to cards oriented in the vertical position, upright relative to you.
records.text: 3.5. “Ready” refers to cards oriented in the vertical position, upright relative to you.

records.title: “Spent” refers to cards oriented in the horizontal position, sideways relative to you.
records.text: 3.6. “Spent” refers to cards oriented in the horizontal position, sideways relative to you.

records.title: To spend a ready card, turn it 90° until it is fully horizontal.
records.text: 3.7. To spend a ready card, turn it 90° until it is fully horizontal.

records.title: To ready a spent card, turn it 90° until it is fully vertical and upright.
records.text: 3.8. To ready a spent card, turn it 90° until it is fully vertical and upright.

records.title: Power
A card’s “power” determines its success in stealing and fighting.
records.text: 3.17.1. A card’s “power” determines its success in stealing and fighting. See ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL.

records.title: A Unit or Legend’s power is equal to the power printed on the card plus the power of its equipped Gear and any curren…
records.text: 3.17.2. A Unit or Legend’s power is equal to the power printed on the card plus the power of its equipped Gear and any current effect modifiers.

records.title: A Gear’s power modifies the Unit or Legend it is equipped to.
records.text: 3.17.3. A Gear’s power modifies the Unit or Legend it is equipped to.

records.title: Units and Legends inherit power from Gears equipped to them.
records.text: 3.17.3.1. Units and Legends inherit power from Gears equipped to them.

records.title: A Gear’s power is equal to the power printed on the card.
records.text: 3.17.3.2. A Gear’s power is equal to the power printed on the card.

records.title: A Gear’s power is not modified by card effects, unless the effect specifically targets the Gear.
records.text: 3.17.3.3. A Gear’s power is not modified by card effects, unless the effect specifically targets the Gear.

records.title: “Base power” refers to the printed power on a Legend, Unit, or Gear, separate from any applied or inherited modifiers.
records.text: 3.17.4. “Base power” refers to the printed power on a Legend, Unit, or Gear, separate from any applied or inherited modifiers.

records.title: Textbox
records.text: 3.18. ### Textbox

records.title: A card’s textbox contains its card text.
records.text: 3.18.1. A card’s textbox contains its card text.

records.title: A card may have multiple textboxes.
records.text: 3.18.1.1. A card may have multiple textboxes.

records.title: “Card text” may include effect text, reminder text, and flavor text, differentiated by formatting and treatment.
records.text: 3.18.1.2. “Card text” may include effect text, reminder text, and flavor text, differentiated by formatting and treatment.

records.title: “Effect text” is any text on a card that dictates a game effect.
records.text: 3.18.1.2.1. “Effect text” is any text on a card that dictates a game effect.

records.title: Effect text may use symbols or keywords as shorthand for longer effects, conditions, or concepts.
records.text: 3.18.1.2.1.1. Effect text may use symbols or keywords as shorthand for longer effects, conditions, or concepts. See TERMS.

records.title: “Reminder text” reminds you of relevant rules, keyword definitions, or other implied effects.
records.text: 3.18.1.2.2. “Reminder text” reminds you of relevant rules, keyword definitions, or other implied effects.

records.title: Reminder text is not effect text, and does not influence gameplay.
records.text: 3.18.1.2.2.1. Reminder text is not effect text, and does not influence gameplay.

records.title: Reminder text is always italicized and parenthetical.
records.text: 3.18.1.2.2.2. Reminder text is always italicized and parenthetical.

records.title: “Flavor text” is non-gameplay text that adds lore to a card.
records.text: 3.18.1.2.3. “Flavor text” is non-gameplay text that adds lore to a card.

records.title: Flavor text is always italicized.
records.text: 3.18.1.2.3.1. Flavor text is always italicized.

records.title: Card text addresses the player who played the card.
records.text: 3.18.2. Card text addresses the player who played the card. When an effect says “you,” it’s referring to the player controlling the card.

records.title: While a Gear is equipped to a Unit or Legend, that Unit or Legend inherits any text in the Gear’s bottom textbox.
records.text: 3.18.3. While a Gear is equipped to a Unit or Legend, that Unit or Legend inherits any text in the Gear’s bottom textbox. See CARD TYPES > Gears.

records.title: A card can be multiple types simultaneously.
records.text: 4.2. A card can be multiple types simultaneously.

records.title: Legends on the field are both Units and Legends.
records.text: 4.2.1. Legends on the field are both Units and Legends.

records.title: A Legend is only valid in the Legends area or field area.
records.text: 4.4. A Legend is only valid in the Legends area or field area. All other areas (trash, hand, deck, etc.) are invalid areas.

records.title: If a Legend moves to an invalid area, remove it from the game.
records.text: 4.4.1. If a Legend moves to an invalid area, remove it from the game.

records.title: If a Legend moves to an invalid area, any effects that trigger from the card entering the area enter pending.
records.text: 4.4.2. If a Legend moves to an invalid area, any effects that trigger from the card entering the area enter pending. Remove the Legend from the game before you resolve them. See GAME AREAS > Removed from Game.

records.title: You may play a Legend from the Legends area to the field as a Unit by paying its cost.
records.text: 4.5. You may play a Legend from the Legends area to the field as a Unit by paying its cost.

records.title: A Legend played in this way enters in the same orientation as it was when it left the Legends area.
records.text: 4.5.1. A Legend played in this way enters in the same orientation as it was when it left the Legends area.

records.title: A Legend played in this way enters with Lag.
records.text: 4.5.2. A Legend played in this way enters with Lag. See Lag.

records.title: Legends with cost Null ( - ) do not have a cost, and cannot be played to the field.
records.text: 4.5.3. Legends with cost Null ( - ) do not have a cost, and cannot be played to the field. See Cost Value.

records.title: Gear cards can be equipped to your Units and Legends to grant them additional power and/or effects.
records.text: 4.9. Gear cards can be equipped to your Units and Legends to grant them additional power and/or effects.

records.title: To play a Gear, reveal the card to your Rival, pay its cost, and equip it to a friendly Unit or friendly face-up Legend.
records.text: 4.10. To play a Gear, reveal the card to your Rival, pay its cost, and equip it to a friendly Unit or friendly face-up Legend. See Equip.

records.title: By default, a Gear can be equipped to a friendly Unit or friendly face-up Legend.
records.text: 4.10.1. By default, a Gear can be equipped to a friendly Unit or friendly face-up Legend.

records.title: You can only equip Gear to a card in the field or Legends area.
records.text: 4.10.2. You can only equip Gear to a card in the field or Legends area.

records.title: There’s no upper limit on the number of Gears equipped to a single Unit.
records.text: 4.10.3. There’s no upper limit on the number of Gears equipped to a single Unit.

records.title: Gears have two textboxes, referred to as the “top textbox” and “bottom textbox.”
records.text: 4.11. Gears have two textboxes, referred to as the “top textbox” and “bottom textbox.”

records.title: The top textbox contains effects for the Gear.
records.text: 4.11.1. The top textbox contains effects for the Gear. These effects are relevant when you play the Gear, and generally not relevant after a Gear is equipped.

records.title: Effects described in the top textbox apply to the Gear itself, and are not inherited by the Unit or Legend it’s equip…
records.text:
4.11.2. Effects described in the top textbox apply to the Gear itself, and are not inherited by the Unit or Legend it’s equipped to.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Gear’s top text box contains the reminder text “*(Equip to a friendly Unit or face-up Legend.)*” You equip this Gear to a friendly Unit. That Gear cannot be equipped to another friendly Unit, nor face-up Legend.

records.title: The bottom textbox contains effects inherited by the Unit or Legend the Gear is equipped to.
records.text: 4.11.3. The bottom textbox contains effects inherited by the Unit or Legend the Gear is equipped to. Read the bottom textbox as if it's printed on that Unit or Legend.

records.title: Effects described in a Gear card’s bottom textbox apply only to the Unit or Legend the Gear is equipped to, not the G…
records.text: 4.11.3.1. Effects described in a Gear card’s bottom textbox apply only to the Unit or Legend the Gear is equipped to, not the Gear itself.

records.title: A Unit or Legend does not inherit Tags or other characteristics from a Gear equipped to it.
records.text: 4.11.3.2. A Unit or Legend does not inherit Tags or other characteristics from a Gear equipped to it.

records.title: When a Legend or Unit moves to a different area (field, trash, hand, etc.), all of its equipped Gear moves with it.
records.text: 4.12. When a Legend or Unit moves to a different area (field, trash, hand, etc.), all of its equipped Gear moves with it.

records.title: When a Gear moves with a Unit or Legend to an area outside of the field or Legends area, the Gear isn’t equipped to t…
records.text:
4.12.1. When a Gear moves with a Unit or Legend to an area outside of the field or Legends area, the Gear isn’t equipped to the Unit or Legend in that area.

> **EXAMPLE:** An equipped Unit has the effect “At the end of your turn, return this Unit to its owner's hand.” When you move the Unit to your hand, you also move its equipped Gear to your hand. Once the cards are in your hand, the Gear is no longer equipped to the Unit. So, if you play the Unit from your hand next turn, the Gear does not move with it.

records.title: If an equipped Legend moves to an area outside of the Field or Legends area, the Gear follows the Legend to the new a…
records.text: 4.12.2. If an equipped Legend moves to an area outside of the Field or Legends area, the Gear follows the Legend to the new area. The Gear is no longer equipped in the new area, so it stays there when you remove the Legend from play.

records.title: When you bottom-deck an equipped Unit, place the cards at the bottom of your deck in a random order.
records.text: 4.12.3. When you bottom-deck an equipped Unit, place the cards at the bottom of your deck in a random order. Randomize them amongst any other cards bottom-decked at the same time. See Bottom-deck.

records.title: A game area may be “public” or “hidden.”
records.text: 5.3. A game area may be “public” or “hidden.”

records.title: If a game area is public, these rules apply.
records.text: 5.3.1. If a game area is public, these rules apply.

records.title: Face-up cards in a public area are known to all players.
records.text: 5.3.1.1. Face-up cards in a public area are known to all players. You can look at information on all face-up cards at any time.

records.title: Face-down cards in a public area aren’t publicly known.
records.text: 5.3.1.2. Face-down cards in a public area aren’t publicly known. You can’t look at them unless directed by an effect.

records.title: If a game area is hidden, these rules apply.
records.text: 5.3.2. If a game area is hidden, these rules apply.

records.title: Cards in a hidden area aren’t publicly known.
records.text: 5.3.2.1. Cards in a hidden area aren’t publicly known. You can’t look at them unless directed by an effect.

records.title: If a card enters a hidden area, ignore any information on the card and remove any existing modifiers attached to it.
records.text: 5.3.2.2. If a card enters a hidden area, ignore any information on the card and remove any existing modifiers attached to it.

records.title: If an effect requires you to reveal and move a card from a hidden area, you must reveal the card before moving it to…
records.text: 5.3.2.3. If an effect requires you to reveal and move a card from a hidden area, you must reveal the card before moving it to another area.

records.title: When you search for a card in a hidden area, you do not have to reveal any information about your findings if you fai…
records.text: 5.3.2.4. When you search for a card in a hidden area, you do not have to reveal any information about your findings if you fail to find a valid target. See Search.

records.title: If an effect requires a player to choose from a hidden area using information that is not public, that player may cho…
records.text: 5.3.2.4.1. If an effect requires a player to choose from a hidden area using information that is not public, that player may choose to fail to find a target.

records.title: If an effect requires you to choose from a hidden area without requiring a qualifying card information, you must choo…
records.text: 5.3.2.5. If an effect requires you to choose from a hidden area without requiring a qualifying card information, you must choose a legal target. You are not required to reveal it.

records.title: If an effect instructs you to look at or search cards in a hidden area and does not say what to do with cards not cho…
records.text: 5.3.2.6. If an effect instructs you to look at or search cards in a hidden area and does not say what to do with cards not chosen, return those cards to their original area in their original order and state.

records.title: Hand
Your hand is where drawn cards are held.
records.text: 5.4.1. Your hand is where drawn cards are held.

records.title: Your hand is a hidden area, but you can freely view its contents and change the order of cards in it.
records.text: 5.4.2. Your hand is a hidden area, but you can freely view its contents and change the order of cards in it.

records.title: You can’t view the contents of cards in your Rival’s hand unless otherwise specified.
records.text: 5.4.3. You can’t view the contents of cards in your Rival’s hand unless otherwise specified.

records.title: You may always know the number of cards in your Rival’s hand.
records.text: 5.4.4. You may always know the number of cards in your Rival’s hand.

records.title: There is no limit to the number of cards allowed in your hand.
records.text: 5.4.5. There is no limit to the number of cards allowed in your hand.

records.title: Field Area
records.text: 5.6. ### Field Area

records.title: The field area may be referred to as just “field” or “your field” (and variations thereof).
records.text: 5.6.1. The field area may be referred to as just “field” or “your field” (and variations thereof).

records.title: Play a card by paying its cost and placing it ready on the field.
records.text: 5.6.2. Play a card by paying its cost and placing it ready on the field.

records.title: All cards played are to the field area unless specified otherwise.
records.text: 5.6.2.1. All cards played are to the field area unless specified otherwise.

records.title: A card in the field is “in play.”
records.text: 5.6.2.2. A card in the field is “in play.”

records.title: The field is a public area.
records.text: 5.6.3. The field is a public area. You can look at the face-up cards any player has on their field at any time. You may always know the number of cards any player has in play.

records.title: Units and Legends enter the field with a condition called “Lag.” See Lag.
records.text: 5.6.4. Units and Legends enter the field with a condition called “Lag.” See Lag.

records.title: There is no limit on the amount of Units you can have in the Field area.
records.text: 5.6.5. There is no limit on the amount of Units you can have in the Field area.

records.title: Legends Area
records.text: 5.7. ### Legends Area

records.title: Each player places their three Legends face-down and randomized in this area at the start of the game.
records.text: 5.7.1. Each player places their three Legends face-down and randomized in this area at the start of the game.

records.title: You can spend any number of Legends in this area as 1 €$ each, whether face-up or face-down.
records.text: 5.7.2. You can spend any number of Legends in this area as 1 €$ each, whether face-up or face-down.

records.title: While you can spend a Legend to pay 1 €$ toward a cost, Legends are not considered Eddies, and cannot become Eddies.
records.text: 5.7.2.1. While you can spend a Legend to pay 1 €$ toward a cost, Legends are not considered Eddies, and cannot become Eddies.

records.title: If a face-up Legend does not have a Sell Tag, you may not spend it for 1 €$.
records.text: 5.7.2.2. If a face-up Legend does not have a Sell Tag, you may not spend it for 1 €$.

records.title: “Call a Legend” may be used only once per turn even if a game action tells you to “Call a Legend”.
records.text: 5.7.3. “Call a Legend” may be used only once per turn even if a game action tells you to “Call a Legend”.

records.title: The Legends area is a public area.
records.text: 5.7.4. The Legends area is a public area. Players can count the number of cards any player has in this area and read them at any time.

records.title: The face-down Legends in this area are hidden.
records.text: 5.7.4.1. The face-down Legends in this area are hidden. You cannot look at them unless specified otherwise.

records.title: If you learn the location of one or more face-down Legend(s), visually distinguish any “known” Legends to your Rival…
records.text: 5.7.4.2. If you learn the location of one or more face-down Legend(s), visually distinguish any “known” Legends to your Rival without revealing them. This can be with a token marker, or by physically separating known Legends from unknown Legends.

records.title: If an effect asks you to look at a face-down legend, you cannot look at it again once that effect has resolved, unles…
records.text: 5.7.4.3. If an effect asks you to look at a face-down legend, you cannot look at it again once that effect has resolved, unless otherwise specified.

records.title: You may pay a Legend’s cost to play it from the Legends area to the field as a Unit.
records.text: 5.7.5. You may pay a Legend’s cost to play it from the Legends area to the field as a Unit. See CARD TYPES > Legends.

records.title: A Legend in the Legend area may use its [Spend Icon] at any point it is face-up in the Legend’s area.
records.text: 5.7.6. A Legend in the Legend area may use its [Spend Icon] at any point it is face-up in the Legend’s area.

records.title: There is no limit of cards that can be in the Legends area.
records.text: 5.7.7. There is no limit of cards that can be in the Legends area.

records.title: Trash Area
records.text: 5.9. ### Trash Area

records.title: The trash area is also referred to as just “the trash” or “your trash” (and variations thereof).
records.text: 5.9.1. The trash area is also referred to as just “the trash” or “your trash” (and variations thereof).

records.title: The trash is a public area.
records.text: 5.9.2. The trash is a public area.

records.title: Cards in this area are placed face-up in a pile, and either player can freely view the contents and order of these ca…
records.text: 5.9.3. Cards in this area are placed face-up in a pile, and either player can freely view the contents and order of these cards.

records.title: When placing new cards in this area, they are placed on top of the previous card already in the pile.
records.text: 5.9.4. When placing new cards in this area, they are placed on top of the previous card already in the pile.

records.title: If multiple cards enter this area at the same time, their owner adds them in any order.
records.text: 5.9.4.1. If multiple cards enter this area at the same time, their owner adds them in any order.

records.title: Players may freely change the order of cards in their own trash.
records.text: 5.9.4.2. Players may freely change the order of cards in their own trash. The cards in the trash should always remain in the face-up position unless specified otherwise.

records.title: Removed from Game
records.text: 5.13. ### Removed from Game

records.title: Cards removed from the game are public, and either player can freely view this area and order.
records.text: 5.13.1. Cards removed from the game are public, and either player can freely view this area and order.

records.title: Cards removed from the game do not have a designated game area, because they are no longer part of the game.
records.text: 5.13.2. Cards removed from the game do not have a designated game area, because they are no longer part of the game.

records.title: When a card you own is removed from the game, designate a “removed” pile outside of the game areas.
records.text: 5.13.2.1. When a card you own is removed from the game, designate a “removed” pile outside of the game areas. Place any removed cards that you own face-up in this pile. This pile can be anywhere, as long as it is clearly visible to both players and doesn’t cause confusion with any game areas.

records.title: A card removed from the game cannot re-enter the game area unless an effect specifically returns the card to the game.
records.text: 5.13.2.2. A card removed from the game cannot re-enter the game area unless an effect specifically returns the card to the game.

records.title: Play a Card
records.text:
8.13. ### Play a Card

As an action during your Main phase, you may play a card from your hand. See Play.

records.title: Cost
A “cost” details what you must pay to play a card, activate an effect, or perform a game action.
records.text: 11.1.1. A “cost” details what you must pay to play a card, activate an effect, or perform a game action. See Pay.

records.title: To play a card, you must pay its cost value in the top left corner of the card.
records.text: 11.1.1.1. To play a card, you must pay its cost value in the top left corner of the card. See Cost Value.

records.title: An activation cost is a cost that must be paid to activate an effect.
records.text: 11.1.1.2. An activation cost is a cost that must be paid to activate an effect. See EFFECTS > Activated Effects.

records.title: A cost must be paid in full; if you cannot pay all required costs, you cannot play the card, activate the effect, nor…
records.text: 11.1.2. A cost must be paid in full; if you cannot pay all required costs, you cannot play the card, activate the effect, nor perform the game action associated with it

records.title: If a cost is replaced by another cost, pay the replacement cost instead of the original cost.
records.text: 11.1.2.1. If a cost is replaced by another cost, pay the replacement cost instead of the original cost. The replacement cost must be paid in full.

records.title: Play
To play a card, reveal it, pay its cost, and then follow the rules for playing that specific card type detailed in {C…
records.text: 11.4.1. To play a card, reveal it, pay its cost, and then follow the rules for playing that specific card type detailed in CARD TYPES.

records.title: If you can’t pay for or follow the rules for playing the card, you cannot play it.
records.text: 11.4.1.1. If you can’t pay for or follow the rules for playing the card, you cannot play it. It’s considered “invalid” to play.

records.title: If you play or attempt to play an invalid card, undo the play attempt and return the game to the previous legal game…
records.text: 11.4.1.2. If you play or attempt to play an invalid card, undo the play attempt and return the game to the previous legal game state as much as possible.

records.title: You can only play cards from your hand unless an effect instructs otherwise.
records.text: 11.4.2. You can only play cards from your hand unless an effect instructs otherwise.

records.title: Effects that allow a player to play a card follows the normal rules for playing that card unless the effect instructs…
records.text: 11.4.3. Effects that allow a player to play a card follows the normal rules for playing that card unless the effect instructs otherwise.

records.title: Equip
“Equip” is a game action in which you attach a Gear to a Unit or Legend by placing the card beneath it.
records.text: 11.6.1. “Equip” is a game action in which you attach a Gear to a Unit or Legend by placing the card beneath it. When you do, the Gear becomes “equipped to” that card. See CARD TYPES > Gear.

records.title: When a Gear is equipped make sure only the bottom text box is showing under the equipped card.
records.text: 11.6.1.1. When a Gear is equipped make sure only the bottom text box is showing under the equipped card.

records.title: Gear stays equipped unless it (or the Unit/Legend it’s equipped to) is defeated or moves outside of the Legends area…
records.text: 11.6.1.2. Gear stays equipped unless it (or the Unit/Legend it’s equipped to) is defeated or moves outside of the Legends area or field.

records.title: A Unit or Legend with one or more Gears attached is “equipped.”
records.text: 11.6.2. A Unit or Legend with one or more Gears attached is “equipped.”

records.title: A Unit or Legend with no Gear attached is “unequipped.”
records.text: 11.6.3. A Unit or Legend with no Gear attached is “unequipped.”

records.title: Units and Legends inherit all effects in the bottom textbox of their equipped Gears.
records.text: 11.6.4. Units and Legends inherit all effects in the bottom textbox of their equipped Gears.

records.title: Units and Legends gain the power of their equipped Gears.
records.text: 11.6.5. Units and Legends gain the power of their equipped Gears.

records.title: "Move" is a game action in which you unequip a Gear from the Unit or Legend it’s equipped to and equip it to another…
records.text: 11.6.6. "Move" is a game action in which you unequip a Gear from the Unit or Legend it’s equipped to and equip it to another valid Unit or Legend.

records.title: Pay

implementationDecisions.decision: Reveal in hand, exact payment, then an explicit EQUIP continuation chooses a friendly face-up field Unit or Legends-area Legend. The Gear stays the revealed hand source until placed beneath its host in that host area; CARD_PLAYED follows attachment. There is no independently unattached field Gear or separate equip payment.
Derive inherited Gear printed power from the actual attached CardInstances, then add supported persistent modifiers. Preserve null printed power as null; do not infer null arithmetic for Viktor.

Preserve ownership and physical identity. Friendly equip requires common controller and area; ownership need not match. host.attachments is the only stored relation, with derived reverse queries. No control-change operation is implemented.

Played Gear enters ready; host orientation is preserved and does not restrict equip. No invented per-host, named-Gear or Cyberware cap. Explicit unlimited Unit equipment and repeated legal Legend equip support the two-Gear replay.

A trusted departure moves host and attached Gear together, detaches outside field/Legends, then removes an invalid-area Legend while Gear stays. Direct Gear departure removes its relation. Same-owner/controller hand/trash destinations and each owner's removed pile are supported; cross-owner hand/trash destinations require a future explicit effect destination.
Trusted simultaneous trash entry requires caller-supplied exact card order; multiple owners require a future choice protocol. No default order is invented.

Gear retention between field/Legends and randomized group bottom-decking are known rules, but their operations are outside this slice. The Move definition does not itself authorize a new voluntary Main action. No Go Solo, combat, defeat, re-equip or UNEQUIP command is exposed.
